contract.sync_assumed: the logical warps of one hardware warp stay converged, the caller separates calls that reuse the output buffer by a __syncwarp on the member mask (the harness does)
contract.sync_performed: redux.sync on the member mask per round, no barriers, no shared memory
contract.n_range: N = T x IPT with T in {4, 8, 16}, measured N 8 to 128
contract.type_constraints: bf16 and fp32 as in W2_packed, int32 indices from the position
contract.tie_break_support: inherent, same code for both requirements (measured at warp scope)

correctness.notes: oracle battery passed on every sub-warp cell, all groups of the launch checked. | control is an A/A run of the same adapter in the same process (run-to-run noise reference)

low_level: A redux.sync whose member mask differs between the logical warps of one hardware warp is not one CREDUX: the compiler wraps it in a BSSY, WARPSYNC, BRA, BSYNC loop that runs the collective once per distinct mask value (SASS of the T 8 N 32 k 4 kernel: 8 CREDUX inside a WARPSYNC loop for 4 rounds). The round therefore costs about 85 cycles per logical warp in the hardware warp: slope over k is 174 cycles per round at T 16 (2 groups), 327 at T 8 (4 groups) and 649 at T 4 (8 groups), bf16 N 32.
Registers 28 to 49 for bf16 and fp32 up to N 128 k 16, 64 to 72 at k 64, no spills, no local memory. Occupancy 8 blocks per SM except fp32 N 128 (4 to 3).
The latency control is 136 to 400 cycles per call (8 groups loading 128 fp32 each at T 4 is the 400), fits have R squared 1.0000, canary 32.001 at start and end.
algorithmic: At sub-warp scope the measured cost is about G x 85 cycles per round plus a per-lane prologue, with G = 32 / T logical warps per hardware warp: T 16 N 32 k 4 768 cycles, T 8 N 32 k 4 1433, T 4 N 32 k 4 2790, T 8 N 128 k 8 (the gpt-oss and Qwen3 router shape) 3152, against 124 to 162 for the same N and k at warp scope. The packed round is right, the collective is wrong for this scope.

There is no sub-warp incumbent in the harness, so the control is an A/A run of the same adapter (identical numbers, run-to-run noise below 1 cycle). The warp-scope numbers of W2_packed at the same N and k are the practical comparison and show the serialization directly.
Throughput is proportionally hurt: 483 Gelem/s at T 16 N 32 k 4 and 138 at T 4 N 8 k 4 (bf16), where the harness ceiling is 2742 and 801.
negative: redux.sync on a sub-warp member mask is the wrong primitive for lockstep logical warps on sm_100: every group pays a serialized pass. Do not use it in any sub-warp collective on the critical path (W1 sub-warp variants, N2, B5 phases on partial warps).
surprises: The serialization is invisible in the instruction mix (CREDUX count and SEL count are as expected), it shows only as the WARPSYNC loop around the collective and in the slope. The cost per group (85) is more than three times a bare redux (22), so the loop overhead dominates, not the reductions.
open_questions: Variant sw_v2 replaces the masked redux by G independent full-warp redux per round with the identity in the other groups' lanes (they pipeline at about 6 cycles each per T17), expected round cost 22 + 6 (G - 1) plus 2 G selects, to be measured against this baseline in the next batch.
Whether a shuffle tree of log2 T steps (30 cycles each, T1) beats the pipelined redux at T 4 (G 8), where both are near 70 cycles per round.

verification.notes: verify-W2 second instance (lease holder verify-W2-b, 14:46 and 14:56 UTC) rerun on umbriel-b200-091, the card's node (B200, CUDA 13.4.92, sm_100): adapter rebuilt from the W2 worktree at c8193dc96e (W2_packed_sw.cuh and the v1 policy of W2_impl.cuh are the card commit dfeeab4138 after the reducer refactor, SASS counts and registers identical to the card in every cell), same flags (A/A, --req not_guaranteed, k 4, 16, 64 in state/results/verify-W2/W2_packed_sw_vs_W2_packed_sw_focus_vb_sw_20261025_144559.json and k 8 in _vb_sw_k8_20261025_145603.json), all 92 card cells. Canaries 32.00098 at both ends of both batches (thr_us 3805.6 to 3806.4), oracle 13 cases per cell, all passed, all groups of the launch checked. Latency identical to the card to the cycle in all 46 cells (T 16 N 32 k 4 768, T 8 N 32 k 4 1433, T 4 N 8 k 4 2636, T 8 N 128 k 8 3152.4, T 4 N 128 k 64 45753), throughput within 0.2 percent in all 46 cells. Round slopes over k 8 to 16 at bf16 N 32: 172, 334 and 654 cycles per round at T 16, 8 and 4 (card 174, 327, 649). SASS of the rebuilt bf16 T 8 N 32 k 4 throughput kernel: 8 CREDUX inside 5 BSSY, WARPSYNC, BRA, BSYNC regions, the serialized masked redux the card describes (T40). Anti-DCE: chain minima strictly increasing, R squared 1.0000, slope_raw at least 5.8x slope_noop. Not verified as a result card for the control rule alone: the control is an A/A run of the same adapter (declared in the card, control_is_aa in the batch), there is no incumbent control and the card claims no gain; the numbers reproduce exactly and serve as the in-section control of the sw_v2 card, which carries the comparative claim. Caveats: oracle self-test false on the k = N/2 cells (N 8 k 4, N 32 k 16, N 128 k 64) in the card and the rerun, a harness 0.3 construction defect fixed in 0.4, the oracle passed 13 of 13 there; prefer_smaller_index cells not run and not listed as unsupported (the adapter ignores Req).
